name: Wisdom Journal Manager – Research Paper/Process Management
author: Zachary Adam

sections.description:
Wisdom Journal Manager is for small editorial boards (student, department, campus and society journals) that already run a WordPress site and don’t want a separate server, a yearly hosting fee or a long manual.

Watch the 4-minute tutorial: one paper from submission to decision, as the author, the editor and the reviewer see it, then the one page administrators use to set up.

The loop

  1. An author submits through a form on your site without signing up first: manuscript, title page, optional cover letter, declarations and a short checklist. They get a private link to follow the paper and, unless you turn it off, an account to log in later.
  2. Editors see it on the Editor Inbox board with its next action, claim it, invite reviewers by email and follow their progress. Reminders go to reviewers automatically.
  3. Reviewers open their private link (no sign-up needed), accept, read the files and send a recommendation with comments for the author and for the editor.
  4. The editor decides: desk reject, accept, minor or major revision, or reject. A ready-made letter with the reviewer comments opens for editing, then goes to the author, who can upload a revision.
  5. Accepted papers are placed in an issue and published with a clean article page, a PDF download, a “How to cite” reference with BibTeX and RIS downloads, and Google Scholar citation tags. DOIs through Crossref or DataCite are optional.

Set up the way your journal works

Each journal has one “Submission & peer review” box with sensible defaults:

  • Peer review model: double-anonymous (default), single-anonymous or open
  • Article types
  • Submission checklist authors must confirm
  • Declarations: competing interests, funding, ethics approval, data availability
  • Licence: CC BY (default), CC BY-SA, CC BY-NC, CC BY-NC-ND or other
  • Reviewers per paper and review deadline
  • Optional 1–10 score on the review form

A journal page indexes can check

The journal page shows the aims and scope, editorial board, a peer review policy written from these settings, the licence, fees, ISSN and how to submit: what the Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ) looks for. A checklist on the journal screen shows what is missing.

Private by default

Manuscripts are stored privately, not in the Media Library. Reviewers only see files after accepting an invitation, never see the cover letter, and in double-anonymous review never see the title page; file names are replaced. Unpublished papers are invisible to the public. After publication only the final file is downloadable.

Built on WordPress

Journals, issues and papers are normal WordPress content with their own roles (Researcher, Editor, Reviewer), so they work with your theme, backups and users.

Shortcodes

  • [wisdjoma_submit]: submission form (journal_id attribute optional)
  • [wisdjoma_my_submissions]: an author’s submissions, statuses and decision letters
  • [wisdjoma_journals], [wisdjoma_issues], [wisdjoma_papers]: public listings
  • [wisdjoma_search]: search published papers
  • [wisdjoma_author_profile]: an author’s public profile

External services

The plugin only connects to external services for optional DOI registration, and only when an administrator triggers it from the DOI Manager or enables automatic DOI assignment there.

Crossref DOI deposit service

Used to register or update DOIs with Crossref.

Data sent: journal, issue, paper, author and DOI metadata, plus the site owner’s Crossref account credentials.

When sent: when an administrator registers a DOI, retries a deposit, runs a connection test, or has enabled automatic DOI assignment on acceptance or publication.

Terms of service: https://www.crossref.org/membership/
Privacy policy: https://www.crossref.org/operations-and-sustainability/privacy/

DataCite DOI service

Used to register DOIs with DataCite.

Data sent: DOI metadata and the site owner’s DataCite account credentials.

When sent: when an administrator registers a DOI, runs a connection test, or has enabled automatic DOI assignment on acceptance or publication.

Terms of service: https://datacite.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/DataCite_DirectMembershipTerms_20240311.pdf
Privacy policy: https://datacite.org/privacy-policy/
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin from Plugins → Add New.
  2. Go to Journals → Getting Started and follow the checklist.
  3. Create your journal (Journals → Journals → Add New) and review the “Submission & peer review” box.
  4. Share the automatically created Submit Manuscript page with authors.
  5. Give your editors the WJM Editor role. Reviewers are invited by email and don’t need to sign up. Choose how authors and reviewers log in under Journals → Getting Started → Accounts and login.
sections.faq:
Do authors and reviewers need a WordPress account?

They don’t have to sign up. Choose how your journal works under Journals → Getting Started → Accounts and login:

  • Automatic accounts (default, recommended). Authors submit with their name and email, without signing up. They get a private link by email and, at the same time, a normal WordPress account with an email to choose a password, so they can log in later and see all their submissions in one place. Reviewers answer invitations by private link and get an account when they accept.
  • Log in before submitting. Authors must log in or register first (turn on “Anyone can register” in Settings → General). Reviewers still answer by link.
  • Private links only. No accounts are created; everyone uses the private links in their emails.

Everyone uses the same WordPress login page with their own email and password; what they can do depends on their role. Authors see only their own papers and can’t edit them after submitting; reviewers see only papers they were invited to; only editors and administrators manage the journal. After logging in, authors land on My Submissions and reviewers on My Reviews.

What if someone loses their link, password or email address?

Lost links can be re-sent from the My Submissions page, and a lost password is reset with “Lost your password?” on the login page. If an author can no longer get email at their old address, an editor opens the paper, uses Change the author’s email, and the new link is sent to the new address (the old link stops working). Send the author their link again re-sends it to the current address.

Do I need an email service or API key?

No. WordPress sends the emails itself, so it works straight away. But the journal runs on email, and many web hosts send WordPress email badly (it lands in spam or never arrives). Go to Journals → Getting Started → Email and send yourself a test. If it doesn’t arrive, install a free email plugin such as WP Mail SMTP or FluentSMTP and connect the mailbox you want to send from; Getting Started explains the steps. Editors are warned on the journal screens when an email could not be sent, and each paper’s screen lists the emails sent about it.

How do we know an author’s email address is real?

Every link we email to an author carries a confirmation code. When they open it, or log in to their account, the paper screen shows “Email confirmed”. Until then it shows “Email not confirmed yet”, so editors can spot a mistyped address. New accounts can’t be used until their owner chooses a password from the link in their own inbox.

Is there a guide for my team?

Yes: Journals → Getting Started → How it works explains, in plain steps, setting up the journal, adding editors, and what authors, reviewers and editors do, how to publish, who sees what, and what to do when someone loses access.

Do I need a login or membership plugin?

No. Accounts are standard WordPress users, so any login, registration, social login or two-factor plugin works with them if you want one.

Are reviewers reminded automatically?

Yes. Reminders go out once a day through WordPress’s scheduled tasks (WP-Cron), which run when your site gets visits. If your host turns WP-Cron off, ask them to run wp-cron.php regularly; Journals → Getting Started shows whether reminders are running.

What happens to personal data?

Authors’ and reviewers’ names, emails, files and reviews are stored on your site to run peer review. Tools → Export Personal Data includes them. Tools → Erase Personal Data removes reviewers’ names and emails from finished review invitations and deletes the email log; submissions and open invitations are kept as part of the editorial record, and the tool tells you how to remove them. Deleting a paper permanently deletes its files, reviews and history.

Are unpublished manuscripts private?

Yes. Files are stored in a protected folder with random names and are only served after a permission check. On Apache the folder also blocks direct access. Upgrading from 2.2 moves existing manuscripts into private storage automatically.

Does the plugin contact external services?

Only if you use DOI registration and only when you trigger it. See “External services” below.

Where did citation tracking, analytics and the REST API go?

They were removed in 2.3 to keep the plugin focused on running a journal. Data they stored is left in your database.
sections.changelog:
2.4.0

  • New: authors can submit without a WordPress account. They get a private link by email for the paper’s status, decision and revision upload, and can have lost links re-sent. Spam protection: a hidden field, at most 5 submissions per hour per connection and 50 per hour for the whole site. Developers can change the limits with the wisdjoma_guest_submission_limits filter.
  • The submission and My Submissions pages are never served from a page cache, so their forms keep working on sites with a caching plugin.
  • Editors see the submitting author’s name and email on the paper screen and in the inbox.
  • Fix: the paper screen’s Paper Type list now uses the journal’s article types.
  • New: invite any reviewer by name and email. Reviewers accept or decline (with an optional reason), read the anonymised files and submit their review through a private link, without an account. Editors are emailed when a reviewer accepts, declines or submits, and can send a reminder or cancel an invitation.
  • New: the Editor Inbox is a board (New, In review, With author, Revised, Accepted). Each card shows the next action, such as “Invite 1 more reviewer”, “Reviews in: make a decision” or “1 review overdue”. Editors claim papers; a claimed paper’s editor emails go to its handling editor only. Handling editors can be changed on the paper screen.
  • New: Decision box on the paper screen with editable letters for desk reject, accept, minor revision, major revision and reject. Letters include this round’s reviewer comments to the author, are sent instead of the generic status email and are shown on the author’s private page. Developers can change the default letters with the wisdjoma_decision_letters filter.
  • Workflow: papers can be desk rejected straight from Submitted, and a resubmitted paper can be sent back for another revision.
  • New: automatic review reminders. Reviewers who haven’t answered an invitation are reminded after 5 days; reviewers who accepted are reminded 3 days before the due date and 1 and 7 days after it. The handling editor (or all editors) is told after 10 days without an answer and when a review is a week overdue. Each reminder is sent once, only while the paper is under review. A Remind button in the Peer Review box sends one now. Developers can change the days with the wisdjoma_reminder_schedule filter.
  • Getting Started shows whether the daily reminder job is running.
  • Private-link pages are titled “Your submission” and “Review invitation” instead of the submission page’s title.
  • New: the journal page shows what readers, authors and indexes such as DOAJ look for: publisher, ISSN and licence; aims and scope; the issues; the editorial board (lines ending in “:” become groups); a peer review policy written from the journal’s settings; open access, licence and fees; and how to submit, with a Submit button. Each journal can turn the added sections off.
  • New: Publication fees setting per journal.
  • New: a “Journal page” checklist on the journal edit screen shows what is still missing.
  • Fix: classic themes showed the journal’s issue list and details twice.
  • Reviews and revisions sent through a private link no longer fail when the page was left open for more than a day.
  • A double click can no longer store a review twice or answer an invitation twice.
  • Security: authors with the WJM Researcher role could publish a paper themselves, skipping review, which made its manuscript public. Only editors can publish now.
  • WordPress’s Publish button can no longer make a paper public while it is submitted, in review, with the author, rejected or withdrawn; it stays private and the editor is told. Publishing an accepted paper this way is recorded in the workflow.
  • New submissions are no longer put in the journal’s latest issue automatically. The issue list on the paper screen shows only that journal’s issues, including issues still being prepared.
  • A submission or revision whose files can’t all be saved is undone completely, so no half-made papers or stray files are left.
  • Deleting a paper permanently also deletes its review invitations, reviews, history and email log. Reminders are never sent about papers in the trash.
  • Uninstalling also deletes the private manuscript files, all plugin settings and the scheduled jobs.
  • New: WordPress’s personal data tools (Tools → Export Personal Data and Erase Personal Data) cover authors and reviewers without an account. Suggested privacy policy text is added under Settings → Privacy.
  • Fix: in block themes such as Twenty Twenty-Five, journal, issue and paper pages showed an empty “Written by … in” line, a comment form and unrelated “More posts”. They now use a plain template (WordPress 6.7 or later), which can be edited in the Site Editor.
  • New: issue pages list their articles in page order, with authors, pages and DOI, and link back to the journal. Paper pages say where they were published (“Published 3 March 2026 in Journal, Volume 2, Issue 1, pp. 12–28”). Journal pages show the latest articles, including ones not in an issue.
  • Classic themes show journal, issue and paper pages with the theme’s own page layout, so sidebars, breadcrumbs and page titles look like the rest of the site. Fixes a doubled title in OceanWP and narrow pages in Astra. Tested with Twenty Twenty to Twenty Twenty-Five, Astra, GeneratePress, Kadence, OceanWP, Blocksy, Neve and Hello Elementor.
  • Astra and Blocksy no longer show “By admin” on journal, issue and paper pages.
  • New issues are assigned to the journal automatically when the site has only one, and the issue screen warns when no journal is chosen.
  • New: published papers show “How to cite” (APA style, with the DOI link) and offer BibTeX and RIS downloads for Zotero, Mendeley, EndNote and LaTeX. Developers can change the citation with the wisdjoma_citation_html filter.
  • Fix: one-line fields on the submission form were as tall as the abstract box.
  • Error messages after a form is sent are stored on the site; a link can no longer make a plugin screen show someone else’s text.
  • Search engines: journal, issue and article addresses are now /journal/…/, /issue/…/ and /article/…/ instead of /wisdjoma_journals/…/; old addresses redirect permanently, so links, search results and DOIs keep working. Developers can change the words with the wisdjoma_url_slugs filter.
  • Search engines: articles, issues and journals carry schema.org structured data (ScholarlyArticle with authors, ORCID, DOI, licence, pages, issue and journal). Without an SEO plugin, pages also get a description (the abstract for articles) and sharing previews; with Yoast SEO or Rank Math the abstract is offered as the description. Filtered search results are not indexed.
  • Authors’ private page shows the paper’s history (each stage with its date). Reviewers can re-read the review they sent through their private link.
  • Privacy: keywords and subjects of manuscripts that are not published yet no longer appear in the REST API, its search or keyword pages; only editors see them.
  • New: accounts for authors and reviewers, the way most journals work. Choose under Getting Started → Accounts and login: automatic accounts (default; authors get one when they submit, reviewers when they accept, each with an email to choose a password), log in before submitting, or private links only. Private links keep working in every mode, and earlier submissions from the same email are added to the new account. After logging in, authors go to My Submissions and reviewers to My Reviews.
  • New: editors can send the author their link again, or change the author’s email when they can no longer receive mail at the old address (the old link stops working and the new one is emailed).
  • Security: authors with an account could still edit or delete their paper in wp-admin after submitting it. Submitted papers are now locked for their authors; changes go through the editors and the revision upload.
  • Fix: email fields on the submission and lost-link forms were narrower than the other fields.
  • New: Getting Started → Email. Send a test email, see whether an email plugin is handling your site’s mail, and get step-by-step help when mail doesn’t arrive. Editors see a warning on the journal screens when emails fail.
  • New: “Email confirmed” on the paper screen, once the author opens a link we emailed or logs in, and a list of the emails sent about each paper.
  • New: Getting Started has a plain-language guide for administrators, editors, authors and reviewers.
  • Fix: right after activation, the first visit to the site by anyone (for example an author sending a submission) could be redirected to Getting Started and lost. Only an administrator opening an admin screen is redirected now.
  • The paper screen uses the classic editor, so the paper’s boxes (author, peer review, decision) are always visible instead of folded away at the bottom of the block editor. Developers can switch back with the wisdjoma_paper_block_editor filter.
  • The reviewer email field in the Peer Review box is wide enough to show a full address.
  • New: a 4-minute video tutorial on the plugin page.

2.3.0

  • Fix: the Upload button (Manuscript Files) and Invite button (Peer Review) did nothing in the paper editor.
  • Security: manuscripts are now stored privately instead of in the public Media Library. Existing files are moved on upgrade. Authors and reviewers no longer get Media Library access.
  • Reviewers see files only after accepting, never see the cover letter, and in double-anonymous review never see the title page or original file names.
  • Unpublished paper pages are no longer visible to reviewers (they showed author names).
  • New: per-journal “Submission & peer review” settings (review model, article types, checklist, declarations, licence, reviewers per paper, deadline, optional score).
  • New: submission form asks for a separate title page in double-anonymous review and an optional cover letter.
  • New: authors see reviewer comments and the decision in My Submissions and in the decision email, and can upload a revision.
  • New: published papers show the licence, a Download button and Google Scholar citation tags; article pages work with block themes.
  • Removed: citation tracking, analytics, REST API, JATS export, author merging, the Student role (its users become Subscribers) and the Automation, Settings, Security Logs and Plugin Verification pages. Stored data is kept. Getting Started now includes a system check.
  • Fix: authors could change editorial fields (DOI, issue, author list) on their own paper.
  • Fix: editorial notes were visible to authors.
  • Fix: duplicate email to the author on submission; editing an author removed the link to their WordPress account.

2.2.3

  • Automatic citation updates are now opt-in and disabled by default.
  • Namespaced all functions, classes, options, shortcodes, capabilities, hooks and REST routes under wisdjoma.

2.2.2

  • Update compatibility metadata for WordPress 7.0 and add the languages directory.

2.2.1

  • Fix template direct-access guards and tighten JATS REST permissions.

2.2.0

  • DOI Manager: pattern tokens, auto-assign on accept/publish, Crossref and DataCite deposit, batch issue DOIs.

2.1.0

  • Editor Inbox, Getting Started checklist, reviewer access to assigned manuscripts.

2.0.0

  • Peer review, editorial workflow, email notifications, submission portal.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.

short_description: Run a peer-reviewed journal on the WordPress site you already have: submissions, anonymous peer review, decisions, issues and DOIs.
